title: A directory on a disk
question: The same mkdir, on ext4: what does a directory look like on a disk?
text: Call 1, [mkdirat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/sub", 0755)](1): [ext4_mkdir](1:ext4_mkdir) A new directory: an inode, all in one journal transaction. [ext4_init_new_dir](1:ext4_init_new_dir) On a disk, a directory is a file of names: its first block, with its own two entries, "." (itself) and ".." (its parent). [ext4_add_entry](1:ext4_add_entry) The name "sub": into a block of /mnt, the parent.
Call 3, [getdents64(fd, [256], 256)](3): [ext4_readdir](3:ext4_readdir) Listing: read the directory's blocks, entry by entry.
